method: Later-status review supplements the historical episode register. Automatically identified last-confirmed endpoints remain unverified after their final evidence month; grey marks do not assert continuing closure. Separately sourced status observations appear only in their observation month. They do not fill historical gaps, change measured durations, establish exact reopening dates or count as new closure episodes. The October status observations may postdate the original 21 October study cutoff and carry their actual observation dates. Coverage is targeted, not a complete current-status audit of every frontier.

observations.qualification: Status checked on 25 October 2026. This observation does not turn the earlier October 2023 last-confirmed date into a reopening, or establish an uninterrupted operational duration for every checkpoint.

observations.title: Rafah: restricted passenger access with medical exceptions
observations.scope: Rafah passenger crossing; ordinary access remains restricted, with documented exceptional movement
observations.movement: Passenger movement, including coordinated medical evacuation
observations.exceptions: UN reporting documents medical evacuations through Rafah in the reporting period. EU mission data also records controlled passenger movements. These are not evidence of unrestricted passage.
observations.summary: UN reporting covering 29 September–12 October records medical evacuations via Rafah and Kerem Shalom. The earlier resumption of limited operations must not be read as ordinary passenger access having fully reopened.
observations.qualification: The sources describe limited operations and recurrent closures; FCDO Egypt guidance also describes Rafah as closed. No claim is made that all movement was stopped, or that exceptional operations continued every day in October. This point locates Rafah and does not infer the status of other crossings or cargo routes.
